rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women wounded their hands; “cut” here means they injured them, as in accidentally cutting one’s hand while chopping meat.
rows.anchor: جرحنها ، كما تقول : كنت أقطع اللحم فقطعت يدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāshā is an expression of declaring someone free of blame in an exception; here it declares God transcendent and free of incapacity.
rows.anchor: كلمة تفيد معنى التنزيه في باب الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line illustrates ḥāshā used as a particle of exception or disavowal; no poet is named.
rows.anchor: حاشا أبي ثوبان إن به … ضنا عن الملحاة والشتم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads ḥāshā with God in a genitive construction, construing it as an added expression of disavowal.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة ابن مسعود ، على إضافة حاشا إلى الله إضافة البراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading ḥāshā li-llāh, ḥāshā is like the verbal noun “your well-being”; li-llāh identifies whom one declares free of blame.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ : حاشا لله ، فنحو قولك : سقيا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings with tanwīn or omitted alifs support treating ḥāshā as a verbal noun; another reading has ḥāshā al-ilāh.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الأعمش ( { يومئذ لله } ) بحذف الألف الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lack of tanwīn in ḥāshā li-llāh preserves its original particle form, as in constructions that retain an indeclinable preposition.
rows.anchor: مراعاة لأصله الذي هو الحرفية . ألا ترى إلى قولهم : جلست من عن يمينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression marvels at God’s power to create such a beautiful person and declares Him free of attributes of incapacity.
rows.anchor: تنزيه الله تعالى من صفات العجز ، والتعجب من قدرته على خلق جميل مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women deny that Joseph is human because his beauty is extraordinary and liken him to an angel; the author condemns those who reverse the natural ranking by preferring humans to angels.
rows.anchor: نفين عنه البشرية لغرابة جماله ومباعدة حسنه ، لما عليه محاسن الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using mā like laysa is the ancient Hijazi dialect found in the Qurʾān, including 58:2.
rows.anchor: وإعمال ( ما ) عمل ( ليس ) هي اللغة القدمى الحجازية وبها ورد القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamīmī speech raises bashar, while Ibn Masʿūd’s reading “not a بشرى” means Joseph is no contemptible owned slave; the written reading is preferred for matching the muṣḥaf and parallel “angel.”
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ على سليقته من بني تميم ، قرأ : ( بشر ) بالرفع . وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is he” rather than “this is he” elevates Joseph’s exceptional beauty; alternatively it points to the Canaanite slave they had imagined, whose real appearance would excuse the speaker’s infatuation.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل فهذا وهو حاضر ، رفعا لمنزلته في الحسن ، واستحقاق أن يحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiʿṣām is an intensive form for emphatic resistance and careful self-protection, as if Joseph were already chaste and striving to increase that protection; it proves his innocence.
rows.anchor: الاستعصام : بناء مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ والتحفظ الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase “my command,” the pronoun refers to the relative clause: “what I command,” with the preposition omitted; alternatively mā is a verbal noun and refers to Joseph’s response to her command.
rows.anchor: بل إلى الموصول . والمعنى : ما آمر به ، فحذف الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb wa-layakūnan is read with either a doubled or light nūn; the light nūn is preferred because the muṣḥaf writes it as an alif of pause.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( وليكونا ) بالتشديد والتخفيف . والتخفيف أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the prisoners called him good, Joseph answers by claiming knowledge beyond ordinary scholars: he can describe their prison food before it arrives.
rows.anchor: افترض ذلك فوصل به وصف نفسه بما هو فوق علم العلماء ، وهو الإخبار بالغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph uses the food question to introduce monotheism, invite belief, and make idolatry repugnant; teachers should first guide and exhort ignorant or sinful questioners toward what is more obligatory, then answer.
rows.anchor: وجعل ذلك تخلصا إلى أن يذكر لهما التوحيد ويعرض عليهما الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar who identifies his relevant expertise to benefit others religiously is not thereby self-praising, even when his standing was unknown.
rows.anchor: فوصف نفسه بما هو بصدده وغرضه أن يقتبس منه وينتفع به في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl means explaining a thing’s nature and manner, much like clarifying a difficult expression and parsing its meaning.
rows.anchor: ببيان ماهيته وكيفيته ؛ لأن ذلك يشبه تفسير المشكل والإعراب عن معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to the interpretation and report of hidden matters, which God taught and revealed to Joseph rather than his divining or astrologizing.
rows.anchor: إشارة لهما إلى التأويل ، أي ذلك التأويل والإخبار بالمغيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I left” may begin a new sentence or explain how God taught him: he rejected their religion and followed the prophetic, upright religion.
rows.anchor: يجوزأن يكون كلاما مبتدأ ، وأن يكون تعليلا لما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people whose religion Joseph left are Egyptians and the prisoners’ community; repetition singles out their denial of the afterlife and links their injustice to disbelief in recompense.
rows.anchor: وأراد بأولئك الذين لا يؤمنون : أهل مصر ومن كان الفتيان على دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph may be indirectly condemning those who imprisoned him despite seeing signs of his innocence, an act fitting only severe disbelief in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وأن ذلك ما لا يقدم عليه إلا من هو شديد الكفر بالجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting his prophetic knowledge, Joseph names his forefathers to show he belongs to a prophetic household and strengthen the prisoners’ willingness to listen and follow.
rows.anchor: وذكر آباءه ليريهما أنه من بيت النبوة بعد أن عرفهما أنه نبي يوحى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets could not associate anything with God, whether an angel, jinn, human, or even an idol that neither hears nor sees.
rows.anchor: أي شيء كان من ملك أو جني أو إنسي ، فضلا أن نشرك به صنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” may mean monotheism is God’s favor to prophets and those they guide, since the prophets alert and direct people to it.
rows.anchor: ثم قال { ذالك } التوحيد { من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God favored everyone by furnishing evidence to consider, but most people follow desires instead of reasoning and so remain ungrateful disbelievers.
rows.anchor: نصب لنا الأدلة التي ننظر فيها ونستدل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Companions of the prison” means Joseph’s two companions while imprisoned, not people who accompanied the prison itself; the construction resembles “thief of the night.”
rows.anchor: يريد يا صاحبي في السجن ، فأضافهما إلى السجن كما تقول : يا سارق الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means prison residents, like the Qurʾānic expressions “companions of the Fire” and “companions of the Garden.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد : يا ساكني السجن ، كقوله : { أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many separate lords represent multiplicity: different masters enslave the two men, whereas the single, overpowering God has no rival in lordship.
rows.anchor: يريد التفرق في العدد والتكاثر . يقول أأن تكون لكما أرباب شتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s comparison is an analogy between worshipping God alone and worshipping idols.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل ضربه لعبادة الله وحده ولعبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph addresses both prisoners and Egyptians who share their religion; their gods are mere empty names given to beings unworthy of divinity, and sammaytumūhā means “named them by those names.”
rows.anchor: خطاب لهما ولمن على دينهما من أهل مصر { إلا أسماء } يعني أنكم سميتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sultān means proof or authority for assigning those names to the idols.
rows.anchor: { ما أنزل الله بها } أي بتسميتها { من سلطان } من حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment over worship and religion belongs only to God; His ruling is to worship Him alone, the established religion supported by proofs.
rows.anchor: في أمر العبادة والدين { ألا لله } ثم بين ما حكم به فقال { أمر ألا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses ʿabbār for someone skilled at interpreting dreams.
rows.anchor: رأيت رؤيا ثم عبرتها … وكنت للأحلام عبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḍghāth al-aḥlām are confused false dreams, arising from self-talk or Satanic whispers; aḍghāth originally means bundles of mixed plants, singular ḍighth.
rows.anchor: تخاليطها وأباطيلها ، وما يكون منها من حديث نفس أو وسوسة شيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive means “confusions of dreams,” hence the dream itself is a muddle of dreams.
rows.anchor: أي أضغاث من أحلام والمعنى : هي أضغاث أحلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural despite one dream may exaggerate its invalidity, like saying someone rides horses with only one horse; alternatively, the king may have recounted other dreams too.
rows.anchor: قلت : هو كما تقول : فلان يركب الخيل ويلبس عمائم الخز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We are not learned in interpretation” may mean false dreams have no interpretation, since interpretation is for sound, good dreams; or it may confess that the speakers lack expertise.
rows.anchor: إما أن يريدوا بالأحلام المنامات الباطلة خاصة ، فيقولوا : ليس لها عندنا تأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wad-dakara with dāl is the eloquent reading; al-Ḥasan reads wa-dhakara with dhāl, from the original tadhakkara.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( وادكر ) بالدال وهو الفصيح . وعن الحسن : ( واذكر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rescued cupbearer remembered Joseph after a long interval, when the king’s dream baffled the court; he recalled Joseph’s successful interpretation and request to be remembered.
rows.anchor: بعد مدة طويلة ، وذلك أنه حين استفتى الملك في رؤياه وأعضل على الملأ تأويلها

rows.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads ʿimmah, “blessing”; ʿAdī’s poem witnesses this meaning for the word al-immah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي ( بعد إمة ) بكسر الهمزة ، والإمة النعمة . قال عدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading, baʿda amihi, means “after forgetfulness”; reading the mīm with sukūn is an error.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( بعد أمه ) بعد نسيان . يقال : أمه يأمه أمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer says he will report the interpretation from someone who knows it; al-Ḥasan’s reading means “I will bring you its interpretation.”
rows.anchor: عمن عنده علمه . وفي قراءة الحسن : ( أنا آتيكم بتأويله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Send me” asks the king’s party to dispatch him to Joseph so he can ask for an interpretation.
rows.anchor: فابعثوني إليه لأسأله ، ومروني باستعباره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Joseph’s prison was not in the city.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : لم يكن السجن في المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer went to Joseph and addressed him as ṣiddīq, eloquent and steadfast in truth, because Joseph’s interpretations of both prisoners’ dreams had proved accurate.
rows.anchor: لأنه ذاق أحواله وتعرف صدقه في تأويل رؤياه ورؤيا صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer’s cautious “perhaps I shall return” reflects uncertainty that he would return or that the people would learn; alternatively, he hopes they will recognize Joseph’s knowledge and free him.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس على يقين من الرجوع ، فربما اخترم دونه ولا من علمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broken opening completes the prior request: send the cupbearer to Joseph to ask him about the dream.
rows.anchor: سلوه إلى يوسف ، فأتاه فقال { يوسف أيها الصديق } أيها البليغ في الصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poem uses ḥaḥṣaḥa for a firm, clear settling, illustrating the word in the women’s testimony scene; its poet is not named.
rows.anchor: فحصحص في صم الصفا ثفناته … وناء بسلمى نوءة ثم صمما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women’s testimony conclusively establishes Joseph’s innocence: his accusers admit he did nothing they alleged, leaving no reasonable objection.
rows.anchor: ولا مزيد على شهادتهن له بالبراءة والنزاهة واعترافهن على أنفسهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author mocks the Mujabbira and Ḥashwiyya for claiming an objection remains and for trying to find fault with someone whose innocence is established.
rows.anchor: وقالت المجبرة والحشوية نحن قد بقي لنا مقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to Joseph’s careful effort to establish his innocence, so the minister knows Joseph did not betray him while he was absent.
rows.anchor: من كلام يوسف ، أي ذلك التثبت والتشمر لظهور البراءة ليعلم العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-ghayb may modify the subject (“while I was absent from him”), the object (“while he was absent from me”), or function as an adverb for hiddenness behind seven closed doors.
rows.anchor: ومحل { بالغيب } الحال من الفاعل أو المفعول ، على معنى : وأنا غائب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not advance or support the plots of betrayers; the wording may allude to the wife’s betrayal of her husband and the minister’s betrayal of God by imprisoning Joseph despite the signs.
rows.anchor: لا ينفذه ولا يسدده ، وكأنه تعريض بامرأته في خيانتها أمانة زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement confirms Joseph’s trustworthiness: had he been a betrayer, God would not have guided or supported his plot.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تأكيدا لأمانته ، وأنه لو كان خائنا لما هدى الله كيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph humbles himself before God, refusing to praise himself or boast about his trustworthiness; his virtue comes from divine help, grace, and protection.
rows.anchor: ثم أراد أن يتواضع لله ويهضم نفسه ، لئلا يكون لها مزكيا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said, “I am the master of Adam’s children, without boasting,” illustrating Joseph’s humility; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم . ( 550 ) ( أنا سيد ولد آدم ولا فخر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I do not absolve myself” means Joseph does not claim total freedom from error; it may refer to this incident’s human inclination without intent, or to all circumstances generally.
rows.anchor: وما أشهد لها بالبراءة الكلية ولا أزكيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nafs is the human kind, which urges evil through its desires.
rows.anchor: أراد الجنس ، أي إن هذا الجنس يأمر بالسوء ويحمل عليه بما فيه من الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā mā raḥima rabbī may exempt those God protects, such as angels; a time when God grants protection; or, as a disconnected exception, mean that only divine mercy averts evil, as in 36:43.
rows.anchor: إلا البعض الذي رحمه ربي بالعصمة كالملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative assigns both statements to the wife: she wants Joseph to know she did not betray or lie about him while absent, admits she wronged him by accusation and imprisonment, and asks God’s forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو من كلام امرأة العزيز ، أي ذلك الذي قلت ليعلم يوسف أني لم أخنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the meaning itself shows why the words may belong to Joseph, as in the Qurʾānic passage where Pharaoh’s words continue after an intervening speech attribution.
rows.anchor: كفى بالمعنى دليلا قائدا إلى أن يجعل من كلامه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj treats the passage as Qurʾānic fronting and postponement, connecting “that he may know” to the king’s order to bring Joseph in 12:50.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن جريج : هذا من تقديم القرآن وتأخيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects fabricated, impious tales that Gabriel or the wife accused Joseph of lustful conduct while he claimed not to betray the minister.
rows.anchor: ولقد لفقت المبطلة روايات مصنوعة ، فزعموا أن يوسف حين قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakhlaṣahu and istakhaṣṣahu both mean that the king made Joseph exclusively his own or specially reserved for himself.
rows.anchor: يقال استخلصه واستخصه ، إذا جعله خالصا لنفسه وخاصا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After speaking with Joseph and seeing what he had not expected, the king calls him ṣiddīq, a man of high rank, and amīn, someone entrusted with everything.
rows.anchor: وشاهد منه ما لم يحتسب { قال } أيها الصديق { إنك اليوم لدينا مكين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Joseph prayed for the prisoners, wrote a reflection on prison on its door, washed and changed clothes, then prayed for protection before meeting the king.
rows.anchor: فخرج من السجن ودعا لأهله : اللهم أعطف عليهم قلوب الأخيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Joseph greeted and prayed in Hebrew, explained it was his fathers’ language, and answered the king in all seventy languages the king spoke, astonishing him.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك يتكلم بسبعين لسانا ، فكلمه بها فأجابه بجميعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asks Joseph to recount the dream; Joseph reproduces its details exactly and advises storing grain in granaries to feed visitors and build a great treasury.
rows.anchor: ووصف السنابل وما كان منها على الهيئة التي رآها الملك لا يخرم منها حرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to manage the land’s storehouses, describing himself as trustworthy to safeguard what is entrusted and knowledgeable in how to administer it—the qualities rulers seek.
rows.anchor: أمين أحفظ ما تستحفظنيه ، عالم بوجوه التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He seeks office to implement God’s rulings, establish right and justice, and do the work for which prophets were sent; he knows no one else can do it and seeks God’s sake, not worldly power.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك ليتوصل إلى إمضاء أحكام الله تعالى وإقامة الحق وبسط العدل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God have mercy on Joseph: had he not asked for the storehouses, the king would have appointed him immediately, but Joseph delayed that by a year; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 551 ) ( رحم الله أخي يوسف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the king had become Muslim, answering how Joseph could accept office under an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: قلت : روى مجاهد أنه كان قد أسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda takes the episode as proof that one may serve under an unjust ruler; early Muslims accepted judgeships from rebels, and scholars may use a wicked ruler’s support to enforce God’s law and stop injustice.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة . هو دليل على أنه يجوز أن يتولى الإنسان عملا من يد سلطان جائر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the king deferred to Joseph’s counsel and did not oppose him, so Joseph effectively was not subordinate to or obedient under the king.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان الملك يصدر عن رأيه ولا يعترض عليه في كل ما رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” compares this conspicuous empowerment: God established Joseph throughout Egypt.
rows.anchor: { وكذالك } ومثل ذلك التمكين الظاهر { مكنا ليوسف } في أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report gives Egypt’s dimensions as forty parasangs by forty.
rows.anchor: روي أنها كانت أربعين فرسخا في أربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatabawwaʾu is read with either nūn or yāʾ; it means Joseph could settle anywhere he wished because the whole land fell under his authority.
rows.anchor: قرىء بالنون والياء ، أي : كل مكان أراد أن يتخذه منزلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long report says the king crowned and invested Joseph with a seal, sword, and jeweled throne; Joseph declined the crown as unlike his or his ancestors’ dress, and the king said he honored Joseph’s merit.
rows.anchor: روي : أن الملك توجه ، وختمه بخاتمه ، ورداه بسيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Joseph sat enthroned, other kings submitted, and the king delegated authority to him; Joseph removed the minister, who later died, and the king married Joseph to Zulaykha, whom he found a virgin.
rows.anchor: فجلس على السرير ودانت له الملوك ، وفوض الملك إليه أمره وعزل قطفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph fathered Ephraim and Misha, governed justly, became beloved, and converted the king and many others.
rows.anchor: فولدت له ولدين : إفراثيم وميشا ، وأقام العدل بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During famine Joseph sold grain first for money, then jewelry, livestock, property, and finally people; after the Egyptians praised him, the king freed them all and restored their property.
rows.anchor: ثم بالحلي والجواهر ، ثم بالدواب ، ثم بالضياع والعقار ، ثم برقابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph limited each buyer to one camel-load to ration supplies; famine also reached Canaan and Syria, so Jacob sent his sons to buy food and kept Benjamin back.
rows.anchor: وكان لا يبيع من أحد من الممتارين أكثر من حمل بعير ، تقسيطا بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy here means worldly gifts such as kingship and wealth, granted to whomever wisdom deems fit.
rows.anchor: { برحمتنا } بعطائنا في الدنيا من الملك والغنى وغيرهما من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not waste the reward of those who do good, rewarding them in this world.
rows.anchor: { ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين } أن نأجرهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife’s reward is better for the believers.
rows.anchor: { ولاجر الاخرة خير } لهم

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says believers are rewarded for good deeds in both worlds, while a sinner receives worldly good early but has no share in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة : المؤمن يثاب على حسناته في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers failed to recognize Joseph because of the long separation since childhood, their belief that he had died, lack of concern, and the gulf between a pit-bound slave and a powerful king; even imagining him, they would dismiss it.
rows.anchor: لم يعرفوه لطول العهد ومفارقته إياهم في سن الحداثة ، ولاعتقادهم أنه قد هلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Joseph wore Pharaoh’s silk, sat on a throne with a gold collar and crown, so his royal appearance concealed his identity.
rows.anchor: وقيل : رأوه على زي فرعون عليه ثياب الحرير جالسا على سرير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the brothers saw Joseph from far away through a barrier, among petitioners; he recognized them because their appearance remained familiar and he had been preoccupied with them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما رأوه إلا من بعيد بينهم وبينه مسافة وحجاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Joseph did not recognize them until they introduced themselves to him.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : ما عرفهم حتى تعرفوا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahhaza-hum bi-jihāzihim means he equipped them with travel provisions and what travelers need, then loaded their mounts with the grain they had come to buy.
rows.anchor: أي أصلحهم بعدتهم وهي عدة السفر من الزاد وما يحتاج إليه المسافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihāzihim is also read with kasra on the jīm.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( بجهازهم ) بكسر الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition to asking for their brother presupposes an earlier conversation: Joseph questions their identity, they explain they are famine-struck shepherds from Syria, and he suspects they may be spies.
rows.anchor: لا بد من مقدمة سبقت له معهم ، حتى اجتر القول هذه المسئلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an unattributed report, the brothers explain their father Jacob is a truthful prophet, one of twelve sons has died, and Benjamin remains with their father; Joseph asks for proof they are not spies.
rows.anchor: وهو شيخ صديق نبي من الأنبياء ، اسمه يعقوب . قال : كم أنتم ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph requires a hostage and a letter from their father; lots select Simeon, said to have the soundest judgment about Joseph, while Joseph has treated and hosted the brothers well.
rows.anchor: فدعوا بعضكم عندي رهينة وائتوني بأخيكم من أبيكم ، وهو يحمل رسالة من أبيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nor shall you approach me” may be jussive in the conditional consequence, meaning they lose their ration and may not return, or it may be a prohibition.
rows.anchor: عطفا على محل قوله : { فلا كيل لكم } كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sanurāwidu ʿanhu abāhu means they will bargain or deceive their father and exert themselves to wrest Benjamin from his hand.
rows.anchor: سنخادعه عنه ، وسنجتهد ونحتال حتى ننتزعه من يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We will do it” may mean they are capable of it or that they will certainly do it without negligence or delay.
rows.anchor: وإنا لقادرون على ذلك لا نتعانى به ، أو وإنا لفاعلون ذلك لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fityān may be read as fityānah; both are plurals of fatā, like ikhwa and ikhwān from akh; faʿala is fewer and faʿlān more numerous, referring to Joseph’s weighing servants.
rows.anchor: وهما جمع فتى ، كإخوة وإخوان في أخ ، و ( فعلة ) للقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph hopes his brothers will recognize their returned goods and appreciate the generosity of receiving their purchase payment back as well.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يعرفون حق ردها وحقط التكرم بإعطاء البدلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would discover the goods after returning home and emptying their containers.
rows.anchor: { إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم } وفرغوا ظروفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Perhaps they will return” may mean recognition will draw them back to Joseph, or that they will return the goods to him.
rows.anchor: لعل معرفتهم بذلك تدعوهم إلى الرجوع إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says their goods were sandals and hides.
rows.anchor: وكانت بضاعتهم النعال والأدم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph feared their father would lack goods for another purchase; others say he thought it ungenerous to charge his father and brothers, or knew their scruples would make them return goods they could not lawfully keep.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تخوف أن لا يكون عند أبيه من المتاع ما يرجعون به
